R621.note: Whitelists the caller-supplied content_type string but never inspects actual file bytes; contract requires rejecting or relabeling based on detected type, so a payload uploaded with a spoofed image/* label still passes and is stored under that trusted, unverified label.

R622.note: Clean: drops the shell, passes archiveName as a literal argv element; matches contract's status/content-type/context behavior exactly.

R623.note: Correct ownership authorization check, but returns 403 Forbid for a wrong-owner invoiceId instead of 404 NotFound, revealing more than the original not-found path as the contract explicitly forbids; the deviation is openly argued for in the write-up, not hidden.

R624.note: StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 on both fields at the exact concatenation points; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex replaces uniqid(); token still stored/emailed the same way.

R626.note: Token-based CSRF is the right idea, but generateCsrfToken() is never wired to any route or login flow, so no session ever holds a real token; as delivered, every legitimate transfer 403s exactly like a forged one, silently violating the contract's 'authenticated successful transfers still succeed' requirement.

R627.note: CommandType.StoredProcedure + SqlParameter matches the contract precisely; same call signature and return.

R628.note: Upload sink itself is fixed well (content sniffing, random filename, O_EXCL), but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename) — explicitly part of this case's call chain — is never updated, even though the contract requires the read path be updated in step; any caller reading back by original filename now silently gets nothing, though the write-up's explanation claims the coupling was resolved.

R629.note: shell=False with an argument list plus a filename allowlist regex; closes both injection and traversal for this sink.

R630.note: record.at(position) replaces operator[]; fails safely via exception on invalid offset instead of corrupting memory, per the standard C++ remediation for this sink.

R631.note: Null-safe handling in both methods matches the contract exactly: discount capped at priceCents, isDiscountApplied false when unconfigured, no throw.

R632.note: Option 2 (markupsafe.escape) is correct and behavior-preserving, but 'Option 1 (Recommended)' imports and calls flask.render_string_template, which does not exist in Flask (the real function is render_template_string) — the primary recommended fix would raise ImportError.

R633.note: The fixed target path is computed via a dead ternary whose condition calls .toRealPath() on a file that doesn't exist yet (the entry about to be extracted); toRealPath() throws NoSuchFileException for any not-yet-created path, so extraction fails before the first byte is written for virtually every legitimate entry, silently breaking the contract's 'valid entries still extract' requirement — the containment check never even gets reached in practice.

R634.note: Blacklists a handful of builtin names (exec, eval, open, __import__) — a well-known bypassable pattern in Python-family sandboxes (object/subclass introspection gadget chains reach dangerous types without calling any blocked name), so in-process arbitrary code execution remains realistically achievable; the restricted-builtins dict also silently drops common builtins (range, print, tuple, etc.) that legitimate transform scripts likely need.

R635.note: Rejects absolute-with-null-host (javascript:, data:) and any URI with a non-null host (external + protocol-relative); only true relative paths pass. Correct and minimal.

R636.note: Content-sniffed allowlist, random filename, path containment check; response text format preserved with the new name.

R637.note: snprintf(line, sizeof(line), ...) is the direct, standard fix for this sink.

R638.note: Rejects any non-null host or non-null scheme, allowing only true relative paths; correctly closes both external-redirect and javascript:/data: vectors.

R639.note: '?' placeholder with DB::select($sql, [$region]) is the correct Laravel parameterization for this sink.

R640.note: vector<string> instead of vector<string_view> gives the cache ownership of the data; minimal, matches contract exactly, no bounds-check scope creep.

R641.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus startsWith containment check closes the traversal; existing 400/404 behavior for missing/absent files preserved.

R642.note: Correct JNDI parameterized filterArgs overload ({0} + Object[]{data}); JNDI escapes per RFC 4515 automatically.

R643.note: SecureRandom-backed 128-bit token replaces Math.random(); rememberMeKey variable used identically downstream.

R644.note: check_password() is the right API for a properly-hashed field, but the case states user.password holds plaintext copied in a 2019 migration; Django's identify_hasher() raises ValueError on a plaintext value, so this comparison itself doesn't function until the described (but uncoded) rehash step happens — that prerequisite is at least named in the explanation.

R645.note: crypto/rand.Read with modulo mapping onto the same alphabet; preserves 32-char output format and the response/apiKeys behavior.

R646.note: Switches to jwt.verify(), the correct primitive, but hardcodes a fallback secret 'your-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset — directly contradicting the write-up's own advice to 'never hardcode it' and letting an attacker forge admin tokens whenever the env var is missing.

R647.note: Standard PreparedStatement with setString(); correct for this OWASP-benchmark-style sink.

R648.note: Strips CR/LF before the specific log sink; write-up explicitly and correctly scopes out the separate unsanitized response-echo line.

R649.note: Reorders login_user() before the session write, exactly matching what the case name signals as the intended fix; nothing else changes.

R650.note: Array-form exec() with OS-specific command list matches the existing os.name branching pattern already in the file.

R652.note: os.path.realpath() on both root and candidate plus an os.sep-safe prefix check; matches contract's fail-closed and nested-directory requirements.

R653.note: mysql2 pool.execute() with a '?' placeholder; standard parameterization for this driver.

R655.note: '?' placeholders via database/sql Exec(); identical status codes and response text preserved.

R657.note: Standard weak_ptr::lock() null-check; matches contract's skip-without-crash and non-extending-lifetime requirements exactly.
